result.headline: Throttle command dropped to 0 at t=100.5 s with no event; the throttle motor output followed and the aircraft then lost altitude.
result.explanation: A control fault occurred at the throttle/propulsion loop (ch2) at about t=100.4 s. The command went to 0 and the output followed it down to 1100 us. The recording does not show who or what commanded it.

evidence.quote: CONSTANT propulsion.throttle was varying, then held 0 from t=100.478 s to the end of the recording (14.044 s, 38 samples)
evidence.shows: Throttle dropped from about 55% to 0 and stayed there to the end, with no event or mode change.

evidence.quote: CONSTANT actuator.output[ch[2]] was varying, then held 1100 from t=100.712 s to the end of the recording (13.749 s, 43 samples)
evidence.shows: The propulsion output went to its minimum and froze, following the throttle command.

evidence.quote: ROLE actuator.output[ch[2]] follows propulsion.throttle (correlation 0.998 over the recording): it serves that loop
evidence.shows: ch2 is the propulsion channel. Correlation was 0.996 at 0 s lag before the drop, so the output tracked its command until then.

evidence.quote: SHIFT actuator.output[ch[1]] changed level for good at t=104.974 s: median 1501 before, 1341 after us (13.3x its variation before)
evidence.shows: The pitch-loop channel moved about 4.5 s after the throttle loss, together with a pitch setpoint shift and falling altitude.

checked.check: Which signals left baseline first from t=95 to 114
checked.result: ch2 left baseline at 100.409 s and throttle at 100.478 s. ch1 followed at 105.62 s, and pitch setpoint at 107.259 s. The first two are within one sample interval, so their order is not separable.
Throttle median 53 -> 0 and ch2 1520 -> 1100, both frozen with zero spread. Other outputs did not freeze.

checked.check: Throttle vs ch2 relation before the drop
checked.result: Correlation 0.996 at lag 0.0 s. The output obeyed its command, so the ch2 output stage itself is not the first sign.
Only two start-up events at t=0.387 s (low voltage warning, sensor health error). Nothing near the throttle drop: no failsafe, no mode change.
ch1 1490 -> 1354 us, pitch tracking error x2.52, yaw tracking x2.74, with the pitch setpoint shifting. ch1 follows the pitch setpoint (line 31), so this is a consequence of the thrust loss.
Altitude fell from 49.748 m at 86.006 s to 38.291 m at the end, and the pitch setpoint rose to 18.63 deg against attitude of 5.319 deg.
No earlier cases in the workspace.

effects.quote: SHIFT actuator.output[ch[1]] changed level for good at t=104.974 s: median 1501 before, 1341 after us (13.3x its variation before)
effects.why: The pitch channel follows the pitch setpoint, which moved after the thrust loss.

effects.quote: SHIFT vehicle.altitude[relative] changed level for good at t=105.184 s: median 50.59 before, 45.194 after m (4.1x its variation before)
effects.why: Altitude loss after propulsion was commanded to zero.

effects.quote: SHIFT control.attitude_setpoint[pitch] changed level for good at t=105.102 s: median -3.74 before, 12.23 after deg (5x its variation before)
effects.why: The controller is asking for more pitch to compensate. Pitch tracking worsens (a11).

data_requests.what: Full autopilot log: flight mode, RC inputs, failsafe flags, battery voltage/current, ESC telemetry
data_requests.why_needed: Settles whether the throttle zero was commanded by mode/operator, by controller logic, or by a power problem.

unobservable.fact: Whether the motor/ESC physically stopped, and the motor/ESC state
unobservable.why_it_matters: Separates a commanded throttle cut from a motor or ESC fault.
unobservable.how_to_observe: Read ESC telemetry or logs; inspect the motor, ESC and wiring on the bench.

hypotheses.claim: Throttle command was set to 0 upstream of the output, so ch2 followed it down and held 1100 us.
hypotheses.because: Throttle dropped to 0 at 100.478 s and ch2 followed (correlation 0.996, lag 0), with no event or mode change recorded.
hypotheses.observed_at: controller throttle command and ch2 output

hypotheses.claim: The motor or ESC failed, and the throttle was then cut or reduced.
hypotheses.because: No motor or ESC signal is recorded; the ch2 output followed its command, so the hardware cannot be judged from this data.

hypotheses.claim: A mode switch, failsafe or operator action commanded throttle 0.
hypotheses.because: No event or mode change is recorded near the drop, but mode and RC input are not in this recording, so it is not excluded.

hypotheses.claim: A power problem such as low voltage forced throttle down.
hypotheses.because: Only a start-up low-voltage warning at 0.387 s; no battery signal and no later warning. Not excluded because voltage is not recorded.

hypotheses.claim: A fault in the pitch loop caused the late pitch tracking loss.
hypotheses.because: ch1 follows the pitch setpoint, and both moved 4.5 s after the throttle loss while altitude fell: a consequence of thrust loss.

events.what: Throttle held at 0 from t=100.478 s
events.why: Output of the propulsion loop; earliest sign with no recorded trigger.

events.what: ch2 propulsion output dropped to 1100 us and held
events.why: Follows the throttle command at lag 0; the output stage obeyed.

events.what: ch1 shift, pitch setpoint change and altitude loss after t=104
events.why: Controller and aircraft responding to lost thrust.

events.what: Roll and yaw tracking divergences at 6-13 s
events.why: Early manoeuvre-time tracking errors; they recover and are not tied to the late fault.

events.what: Start-up low-voltage warning and sensor health error at 0.387 s
events.why: Start-up lines; nothing later in the data points back to them.

result.lesson: No earlier cases exist in the workspace, so none apply.
result.reuse_when: Same airframe/autopilot where a propulsion output (throttle channel) drops to minimum and freezes, with no failsafe or mode event logged and the output still tracking its command.
